NOTES TO THE STANDALONE FINANCIAL RESULTS – Q2 FY27


1. The above results were reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at its meeting held on 11th November 2026.

2. The Company supplied power from the Mundra Power Plant ("Plant") upto 30th June 2025, based on the directions of the Ministry of Power (‘MoP’) under Section 11 of the Electricity Act, 2003, since 16th April, 2023. Effective 3rd July 2025, the Company temporarily suspended operations of the Plant to undertake pending overhauling activities aimed at resolving existing technical issues. On 23rd March 2026, with effect from 1st April 2025, the Company executed the supplementary power purchase agreement (‘SPPA’) with Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (‘GUVNL’), with revised tariff and power supply framework, which superseded the earlier PPA for GUVNL’s contracted capacity. While approvals from the remaining procurers are in progress, the MoP issued directions under Section 11 on 22nd March 2026, permitting plant operations from 1st April 2026 to 30th June 2026 with the terms of SPPA which was extended up to 30th September 2026 by way of directions issued on 19th June 2026. Further on 25th September 2026, such directions have been extended till 31st December 2026. Management expects completion of the SPPA with the other procurers during this period.

3. On 26th September 2023 the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (‘SIAC’) published a liability award whereby the SIAC held that the Company was in breach of certain clauses of the Non-disclosure agreements entered into with Kleros Capital Partners Limited ('Kleros') and of its contractual duty of good faith and confidence. Further, on 1st July 2025 and 27th August 2025, the SIAC published a quantum award and final award (together referred to as 'Awards'), directing the Company to pay Kleros damages for loss of opportunity of USD 490.32 million with simple interest of 5.33% from 30th November 2020 and cost of SGD 11.34 million with simple interest of 5.33% from 1st July 2025.

On 23rd October 2025, the Company had challenged the Awards before the Singapore International Commercial Court (‘SICC’) by filing applications to set aside the Awards. However, on 26th August 2026, the SICC dismissed the Company's applications to set aside these Awards (’SICC Award’), concluding that the SIAC had considered and determined the relevant issues and that there was no basis for the SICC to re-examine those matters. Further, the SICC passed judgments on 17th September 2026 and 18th September 2026, for enforcement of the Quantum Award and the Final Award respectively. The Company has filed notices of appeal against the SICC Award before the Singapore Court of Appeal (‘Apex Court’) on 7th September 2026 which were accepted on 15th September 2026. Pursuant to the directions issued by the Court, the Company is required to file its written submissions by 23rd November 2026, Kleros is required to file its submissions by 14th December 2026, and the Company is required to file its reply submissions by 24th December 2026. The appeal has been listed for hearing on 19th January 2027.

Subsequently, in an ex parte application filed by Kleros before the SICC, an order dated 26th October, 2026 was passed directing officers of the Company to appear before the Registrar on 8th December 2026 and provide details of the Company's assets. Pursuant thereto, on 6th November 2026, notices were served on the Company's wholly owned Singapore subsidiaries, Tata Power International Pte. Limited and Bhira Investments Pte. Limited, intimating attachment of the Company's shareholding in the aforesaid entities by the Court-appointed Sheriff (Enforcement Officer) upto the value of SGD 830.77 million. The Sheriff also served a copy of the aforesaid order passed by the SICC. The Company's shareholding in these entities is pledged in favour of the consortium of lenders of the respective subsidiaries. The Company is in process of filing an objection to Enforcement proceedings. If Kleros disputes the grounds of objection, the Sheriff will direct the objector to file an application for release of the Shares. The Sheriff can only commence the sale or delivery process of the Shares after the Release Application is decided by the SICC which is further appealable. Pending the adjudication of the appeal before the Court of Appeal, the Company will also seek deferment of sale of shares from the Sheriff.

Based on the legal advice, the Company continues to retain control over the financial and operating policies of these subsidiaries and also continues to have economic benefits arising from these subsidiaries and the Enforcement Order will only enable the Sheriff to sell these shares subject to the procedure as described above.



Based on the legal advice received and the assessment of management duly approved by the Board of Directors, the Company believes it has a high probability of succeeding on its grounds of appeal before the Apex Court, and hence the entire enforcement proceedings will become redundant.

Accordingly, the Company has concluded that no provision is required to be recognised in the financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026.

4. During the quarter, the Company's shareholding in Tata Projects Limited (‘TPL’), an associate, reduced from 22.70% to 19.31% pursuant to rights issue raised by the associate, in which the Company did not participate. Following the reduction in shareholding and reassessment of the rights and obligations under the applicable shareholder arrangements, the Company concluded that it no longer has significant influence over TPL in accordance with Ind AS 28, Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures. Accordingly, TPL ceased to be an associate of the Company from 11th September 2026 the date from which significant influence was determined to have ceased and the resulting gain arising from derecognition being amounting to INR 99.63 crore and tax expense of INR 14.25 crore has been recognized as an Exceptional item.

5. During the quarter, the Company reassessed the classification of certain expenditure relating to its Slum Rehabilitation Authority (‘SRA’) project at Trombay, Chembur. Following completion of the rehabilitation phase and handover of rehabilitation units to the eligible occupants, management reviewed the intended use of the remaining development rights, land benefits and free sale FSI associated with the project. Based on the revised business strategy, the Company intends to hold these assets for long-term capital appreciation and future economic benefits rather than development of a residential building and sale of units. Accordingly, pursuant to the requirements of Ind AS 40 – Investment Property, and upon evidence of a change in use, INR 582.38 crore has been reclassified from Inventories – “Properties Under Development” to Investment Property at cost. Based on an independent valuation carried out, the fair value of the above Investment property was assessed to be lower than its carrying amount and, accordingly, the Company has recognised an impairment provision of INR 102.28 crore and tax income of INR 25.75 crore on above loss has been recognised, which has been disclosed as an Exceptional Item.



Debt Equity Ratio: Total Debt /Total Shareholder's Equity

Total Debts - Long term borrowings (including current maturities of long term borrowings), lease liabilities (current and non current), short term borrowings and interest accrued on these debts.

Total Shareholder's equity - Issued share capital and other equity.

Debt Service Coverage Ratio(not annualised):

(Profit before exceptional items and tax + interest expenses + depreciation and amortisation-current tax expense)/
(Interest expense + scheduled principal repayment of long-term debt and lease liabilities during the period)

For the purpose of computation, scheduled principal repayment of long-term borrowings does not include prepayments(including prepayment by exercise of call / put option).

Interest Service Coverage Ratio:

(Profit before exceptional items and tax + interest expense) / Interest expense
